title: fix(2d): Side Auto reads the material at the picked ring's own level
body:
Stacked on #1935. The base branch is `issue/1927-contour-outside-hole-refusal`.

## What changed

- Side Auto of a 2D Contour on picked rings now reads the part section at the rings' own level. It does not read the full XY silhouette. The floor of a blind bore filled that silhouette, so Auto resolved Outside on the bore rim and the #1927 law refused the pass.
- New law `machining2d::auto_side` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_auto.rs`):
  - It reads the section 0.01 mm under the top of the picks' Z span, then 0.01 mm over its bottom.
  - At each probe it compares the area inside the rings with a 0.5 mm band outside the rings. A side holds material at a fill of 0.5 or more.
  - Material inside only gives Outside. Material outside only gives Inside. The first probe that decides is the result.
  - If the two probes decide differently, or if they see material on both sides and do not decide, the generate is refused by name: "Side Auto cannot tell which side of the picked ring holds the material at Z ...: ... - set Side to Inside or Outside".
  - If no probe sees material on either side (a sheet part, a ring over the part in air), the part's XY outline decides, as before.
- New `crates/app/src/operation/contour_auto_pick.rs`: it reads the Z span of the picks (in the setup frame, or along a tilted frame's axis) and the material, and calls the law.
- `selection.rs` uses the new verdict in place of the old fill block. `generate.rs` refuses an Undecided verdict by name. `contour_auto_side` (the UI preview) maps Undecided to "no answer".
- The rule applies only to `OpParams::Contour` with Side Auto. Plasma and wire contours do not use this verdict.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/1933-contour-auto-side-level.md`.

## Readings (tool centre to the wall, Ø6 tool, Side Auto, model top to model bottom)

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Blind bore rim, Ø20 bore to floor Z 4, rim at Z 10 | Outside, refused "set Side to Inside" | Inside, centre 3.000 mm inside the wall (max error 0.000001), deepest level Z 4.000 (the floor), 0 gouges |
| Same bore, floor rim at Z 4 | Outside | Inside, same pass, deepest level Z 4.000, 0 gouges |
| Through hole Ø20 | Inside | Inside, centre 3.000 mm inside the wall, cut to Z 0, 0 gouges |
| Boss 20 x 20 on a floor at Z 5 | Outside | Outside, centre 3.000 mm outside the wall, cut to Z 5, 0 gouges |
| Block 40 x 40 outer wall | Outside | Outside, centre 3.000 mm outside the wall, cut to Z 0, 0 gouges |
| `Milling-test.step` bore rim r 12.5 at Z 20 (Ø10 tool) | Outside, refused | Inside, the same moves as Side Inside, centre 5.000 mm inside the rim, 0 warnings |

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/contour_auto_level.rs` (new, 3 tests): `auto_on_a_blind_bore_rim_cuts_the_wall_from_inside_to_the_floor`, `auto_on_a_through_hole_rim_cuts_inside`, `auto_on_a_boss_and_on_an_outer_wall_cuts_outside`.
- `crates/motion/tests/contour_auto_side.rs` (new, 6 tests): the law on boxes, the floor rim, the mid-solid refusal, the disagreeing probes refusal, the outline fallback and the empty part.
- `crates/app/tests/area_open.rs`: `a_containment_that_puts_the_tool_in_the_part_is_refused_by_name`. Its last assert now expects the clean Inside pass in place of the refusal.
- The #1935 refusals are unchanged: `contour_outside_hole` 5 of 5 pass.
- `operations.rs` 120 pass, 6 ignored. This includes the sheet-part tests `contour_boss_pick_defaults_outside`, `a_closed_chain_routes_the_boundary_path_not_a_centerline` and `selection_notes_report_stitching_and_extension`.

## Gate

Quick gate on 13a1f2625 (`cargo xtask gate quick`, 36.6 min): post ok (11 s), motion ok (790 s), ui ok (58 s), app FAIL (1328 s) in 2 tests only: `setup_align::unverified_kinds_are_refused_while_verified_picks_generate_aligned` and `stitch_cross::a_self_touching_single_body_still_stops_at_its_top_level`. These 2 tests fail with the same message on the base #1935 head 0761173e8, without this change. They are not caused by this PR. New tests: `contour_auto_side` (motion, 6 pass), `contour_auto_level` (app, 3 pass).

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Two app tests fail on the base branch #1935 (head `0761173e8`) before this change, with the same message. I ran them on the base code to make sure:
- `setup_align::unverified_kinds_are_refused_while_verified_picks_generate_aligned`
- `stitch_cross::a_self_touching_single_body_still_stops_at_its_top_level`

Both fail with the #1927 refusal "meets its wall at no level below the part top". The first has Side Auto, and the Auto verdict there is Outside before and after this change. The second has Side Outside. These failures belong to #1935, not to this PR.

## Not exercised

- Side Auto under a tilted frame (the code reads the frame's local facets; no test).
- Picks at several levels in one op: they share one verdict over their combined span.
- Plasma and wire contours: the verdict is not used there. They lose the note "machining inside the ring - the selection bounds air", which they did not act on.
- The GUI was not started.

Changelog: 2D Contour Side Auto on a picked ring now reads the material at the ring's own level: a blind bore rim is cut from inside, and a ring that Auto cannot read is refused by name.

Effort: high

Fixes #1933

title: feat(gate): one step for each test binary in quick, batch and release
body:
Process change: yes

What changed
- `cargo xtask gate quick`, `batch` and `release` plan one step for each test target of the debug suites, as the heavy lanes do (#1714). Step names: `<crate> suites: lib`, `bins`, `<binary>`, `doc`.
- Batch and release start with one build step (`cargo test --no-run`). Quick builds one time for each crate when the crate has more than one run step.
- Each step has its own log, time and pass or fail line. `--only "app suites: cmds"`, `--failed` and `--dry-run` work for one step.
- Batch keeps `lib` and the binaries, without `SLOW_BINARIES` (as before). Release adds `bins` and `doc`. The ui steps keep CWD `crates/ui`.
- The gate skill, the AGENTS.md tier table and the xtask usage text describe the new steps.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/1941-gate-step-per-binary.md` (steps run in the same order as before; release keeps its waves; a step runs `cargo test -p x --test b`, no direct exe).

Plan sizes (`--dry-run`, this tree)
| Tier | Steps before | Steps after |
|---|---|---|
| batch | 10 | 713 |
| release | 189 | 911 |
| quick (for a diff) | one step for each crate | one step for each target, and a build step |

Measured (Windows, this machine)
- 7 geometry targets, build ready: one grouped cargo call 1.5 s. Seven steps through `cargo xtask gate batch --only "geometry suites"`: 5.0 s. So one cargo start is about 0.5 s. No step rebuilt anything (each ran in 0 s).
- Estimate, not measured: about 6 min more serial time in batch for 713 steps.
- Not measured: a full batch gate before and after (about 20 min each), and any Linux runner time. The release wave parallelism is unchanged.
- Follow-up #1951 (P7): run the exes from the cargo JSON paths to remove the cargo start.

Pinning tests (`cargo test -p xtask`, 141 pass)
- `step_tests::release_runs_every_target_of_every_crate_one_step_each`
- `step_tests::batch_runs_lib_and_each_non_slow_binary_one_step_each`
- `step_tests::only_and_failed_select_one_binary_step`
- Updated: `tests::batch_skips_slow_binaries_and_release_runs_everything` and the quick plan tests.

Test count: no `#[test]` changed in the crates. The step targets of each crate equal the targets of `cargo test -p <crate>` (batch: minus `bins`, `doc` and the slow binaries, as before). The step tests pin this for every crate.

Real runs: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (xtask unit tests, green) and `cargo xtask gate batch --only "geometry suites"` (7 steps, green). Not run: a full batch or release gate; a quick gate over app or ui steps.

title: feat(contour): Start point and Exit point rows on the Lead tab
body:
## What changed
The closed 2D contour already takes a user-set start point (#1478) and exit point (#1492) through the project file and MCP `edit_operation`. The GUI had no door to them. This PR adds that door, as typed coordinates:

- The 2D Contour "Lead in / Lead out" tab has two new optional groups, "Start point" and "Exit point". Each group is switched on in its header, like Plunge and Engagement.
- Each group has an X row and a Y row in model coordinates ("Start X", "Start Y", "Exit X", "Exit Y").
- One visible line under the rows says the safety rule: a point that the lead cannot fit at is refused by name, and the point never moves.
- Off writes `None`, which is the automatic seam (the same as every earlier file). On seeds the model origin.
- The rows edit the draft params. Apply commits them through `EditOperationParams`, so Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y restore the earlier point.
- Other kinds draw neither group. They refuse a point by name (`OpParams::named_refusal`), so a row there could only produce a refusal.

New file `crates/ui/src/egui_app/start_exit_rows.rs` (74 lines) and one call in `approach_page.rs`. No change to the generator, a command, the project file or MCP.

## Images
Rendered with the real page code in an `egui_kittest` harness (a 2D Contour with a start point of X12.5 Y-20 in its params). "Before" is this branch with the one new call removed, which is the page code of main.

Lead in / Lead out tab, before: ![](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/8b952e0f9bdcc7cf4285643e2efad18b14c1a83a/issue-1448/before-lead-tab.png?raw=true)

Lead in / Lead out tab, after: ![](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/8b952e0f9bdcc7cf4285643e2efad18b14c1a83a/issue-1448/after-lead-tab.png?raw=true)

## Tests
New `crates/ui/src/egui_app/start_exit_tests.rs` (4 tests, structural: AccessKit labels, roles, toggled and enabled state):
- `the_contour_lead_tab_has_both_point_groups_off_by_default`: both groups are on the tab, their header switches are off and enabled, the X/Y rows are not in the tree, and drawing the tab writes no point.
- `a_typed_start_point_applies_through_the_history_and_undoes`: the switch seeds (0, 0) and shows the rows and the consequence line. A typed X of 12.5 edits only the draft. Apply commits (12.5, 0) and leaves the exit unset. Undo gives `None` again, and redo gives (12.5, 0) again.
- `switching_the_exit_point_off_clears_it`: a saved exit shows its group on with its rows; the switch off writes `None` and removes the rows.
- `kinds_without_a_picked_start_draw_neither_group`: 2D Pocket and Face draw neither group.

Updated `every_field_lives_on_exactly_one_section`: "Start point" and "Exit point" are on the Contour's Lead tab only.

Readings:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on 91e51a2db: green. ui lib 820 passed, 6 ignored (snapshot lane); `boundary` 3, `boundary_picks` 6, `sinker_setup` 2, `theme_files` 14 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Output with no point set: unchanged. This PR touches no generator, post or project-file code, so the goldens are the same by construction; the gate selected no app, motion or post suite.

## Project file and MCP
- Project file: no new field (the fields shipped in #1478 and #1492). No version bump.
- MCP: no new command. `edit_operation` already takes `links.approach.start_point` and `exit_point`.

## Not exercised
- The pixel snapshot lane (release only; no PNG changed).
- A generate from the GUI after Apply. The generator law for a picked point is pinned by the motion `contour_start` and app `contour_start_point` suites, which this PR does not touch.
- Inch display: the rows use the shared `num` unit lens, the same as every other length row.

## Left for later
#1473 holds the rest: the viewport pick on the wall (item 2), compensation (4), open chains (5), tilted contours (6) and other operations such as the Pocket entry point (7). Item 3 (tabs) is PR #1822. This PR uses `Refs`, so #1448 stays open.

Decision: `docs/decisions/1448-start-exit-rows.md`.

Changelog: The 2D Contour's Lead in / Lead out tab has Start point and Exit point groups, where you type the X and Y at which the cut starts and leaves the closed contour.

Effort: high

Refs #1448

title: fix(geometry): add bounded ASCII DXF reader
body:
## What changed

Add a bounded ASCII DXF reader in `camcraft-geometry`.
Read HEADER, TABLES, LAYER definitions, and basic planar entities.
Keep drawing units explicit and preserve exact lines, circles, arcs, and polyline bulges.
Keep layer names on primitives and count skipped annotations by kind.
Refuse malformed input and unsupported geometry by name.
Add no dependencies.

This branch starts at upstream/main `3580f388821d604e602728495a53df1881889b0d`, as requested for this issue.

## Cause

The geometry crate had no ASCII DXF reader.
Later profile-import work needs shared primitives, explicit units, and input limits.

## Tests

All 30 tests pass in `dxf` and `dxf_refusals`.
The initial tests failed to compile because unchanged upstream had no `dxf` module.
The layer-name limit also had a failing runtime pin before the guard was added.

Named pins include:

- `dxf_rectangle_keeps_layers_and_explicit_units`
- `dxf_missing_unitless_unknown_and_standard_scales_are_explicit`
- `dxf_circle_and_wrapping_arc_stay_exact`
- `dxf_bulge_sign_and_major_arcs_keep_the_exact_sweep`
- `dxf_legacy_polyline_uses_parent_layer_and_closing_bulge`
- `dxf_annotations_are_counted_by_kind`
- `dxf_layer_name_length_is_bounded_before_segment_copies`
- `dxf_declared_vertex_limit_is_checked_before_reading_vertices`
- `dxf_nonfinite_and_out_of_range_geometry_is_refused`
- `dxf_varying_z_within_and_between_entities_is_refused`
- `dxf_input_entity_and_vertex_caps_are_enforced`
- `dxf_deterministic_smoke_fuzz_never_panics`

Copying the actual upstream `lib.rs` back made both suites fail with the missing-module error.
Restoring the reader made both suites pass.

Runtime mutation checks ran 72 experiments.
Seventy experiments failed at runtime and passed after restoration.
Two individual changes remained unobservable:

- `units_missing_at_variable`: the final HEADER check still refuses the missing value.
- `missing_vertex_x`: callers only finish a pending vertex after X is present.

Removing both missing-unit checks failed a pin.
Replacing both pending-coordinate checks also failed a pin.
The missing-X check alone remains unobservable through the public API.
Every restoration passed. No mutation remains in the branch.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all 10 steps.
The geometry change expanded the gate to batch. The run took 42.7 minutes and needed no reruns.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry --all-targets -- -D warnings` also passed.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` has no output.

## Not exercised

This change adds the core reader. GUI import and downstream DXF machining workflows need later integration work.
Windows and macOS builds were not run.
Release-heavy tests and pixel snapshots were not run.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changed the planned files at the overlap check.

Changelog: Add a bounded ASCII DXF reader with explicit units, layers, exact planar primitives, and named input refusals.

Effort: max

Fixes #1860

title: fix(2d): refuse a picked contour ring whose side stands in the part
body:
﻿## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_depth.rs`: new `picked_law`. A picked ring that walks no level below the local part top is refused by name when the operation levels go below that top. The local top is the highest vertex of the facets near the ring (XY box plus the tool radius and the stock to leave).
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour.rs`: new entry point `contour_on_picked`. It runs the law after the depth ladder. `contour_on_part` and `contour_on_bodies` do not change.
- `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`: the Selection source of 2D Contour calls `contour_on_picked`. The whole-model source (entity or stock) does not change.
- `docs/decisions/1927-contour-picked-ring-law.md`: the decision and the dropped alternatives.

The refusal text names the ring position, the part top and the fix, for example: "the picked ring at (0.294, -12.986) meets its wall at no level below the part top Z 10.000: the cutter Outside this ring stands in the part material - if the ring bounds a hole, set Side to Inside; else check the tool containment". The side that the law reads is the resolved side (the app resolves Auto first), and a tool containment also moves the ring. Thus the text names the two causes.

Two existing tests pinned the silent top-plane pass and change:
- `crates/app/tests/area_open.rs`: on the rim of a blind bore, Side Auto resolves to Outside, and a forced Containment Outside puts the ring 10 mm into the wall. The two cases cut only the mouth, in air, with 0 warnings. They are now refused by name. Side Inside is the clean control. The test is renamed to `a_containment_that_puts_the_tool_in_the_part_is_refused_by_name`. The wrong Auto verdict on blind bores is #1933 (P3). This PR does not fix it.
- `crates/app/tests/tilt.rs`: the flat control used Inside on the top face of a block (the mirror case). It now uses Outside.

## Readings (main `d1484f02a`)

- Plate 60 x 60 x [0, 10], through hole D20, D6 end mill, stepdown 2.5.
- Side Outside on the hole wall walked only Z 10 and posted with status Ok, 0 warnings and 0 gouges. Full depth (Bottom of model) gave the same result.
- Cause: the depth ladder reads the material strictly above each level. At the part top no material is above, so each ring is legal there.
- The tip stayed on the top face, so the posted path did not gouge. It machined nothing that the user picked and said nothing.
- `verify` on the same ring forced down the full ladder reports Gouge warnings. The verifier has no gap, so no verifier issue is filed.
- Details are in the issue comment.

## Pinning tests

`crates/app/tests/contour_outside_hole.rs` (5 tests):

- `outside_on_a_picked_hole_wall_is_refused_by_name_at_every_depth` (chain pick and patch pick, full depth and selection heights)
- `inside_and_auto_on_the_hole_wall_cut_every_level_clean`
- `outside_on_an_outer_wall_and_on_a_boss_stays_legal`
- `inside_on_a_picked_block_top_is_refused_by_name`
- `the_full_depth_outside_ring_is_a_gouge_to_the_verifier`

Also pinned: `area_open::a_containment_that_puts_the_tool_in_the_part_is_refused_by_name`, `tilt::tilt_on_a_picked_selection_refuses_by_name`.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick`) on `dfceb20ac`: post suites ok (67 s), motion suites ok (777 s), app suites ok (775 s), 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. `cargo fmt --check` is clean. The branch has a merge of `origin/main` (it takes the #1924 test repair). The last commit is docs only.

## Review fix (head 72c8f293d)

A quick gate on a tree with 0761173e8 had two red camcraft-app tests. On origin/main they cannot fail this way: the refusal text is not in main (`git grep` finds 0 hits).

- `setup_align::unverified_kinds_are_refused_while_verified_picks_generate_aligned`: the refusal is correct. The test picked the first horizontal face, the modelled top annulus (Z 20, hole 20 x 20). The setup flips the part over Y, so the annulus lies at the setup's Z 0 and the blind hole opens down (Z 0..10). Z 10..20 is solid 40 x 40. Outside of the hole ring, the cutter centre runs at +-8 mm, in that solid at Z 16 and Z 12. The old path kept only the top plane, in air. The law reads the setup frame: the same ring generates as modelled. The test now picks the modelled bottom face (the setup's top) with Side Outside and asserts a cut below Z 19.9. The annulus stays as a control: it generates as modelled and is refused by name after the flip. The Offset2D refusal and the Contour1 assert do not change.
- `stitch_cross::a_self_touching_single_body_still_stops_at_its_top_level`: the refusal gave the wrong cause. The ring is Outside of a 40 x 40 outline, and Outside is air. The ladder stopped the ring at Z 10 because the one self-touching shell cannot be sectioned at Z 0 (non-manifold slice error, fail closed). The law said "set Side to Inside", which is wrong advice. Fix: `contour_depth::ladder` keeps the slice error that stopped each ring (`Ladder::unread`). `picked_law` still refuses, but it names that error and the skipped levels, and does not name the side. The test asserts the refusal, `levels below skipped (0.000)`, `non-manifold`, and no Side advice. The one-block reference still cuts below the top.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`) on 72c8f293d: motion suites ok (843 s), app suites ok (785 s), setup_align and stitch_cross ok, 0 failed. Targeted runs: stitch_cross 6/6, setup_align 10/10, contour_outside_hole 5/5, area_open 11/11, tilt 8/8, operations 120/120 (6 ignored). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. `cargo fmt --check` was not run on this head: `cargo fmt -p` fails with os error 206 on this machine.
## Not exercised

- The MCP path and the GUI (the same generator runs under them).
- Multi-body picks with bodies of different heights.
- Auto on a blind bore is pinned as a refusal only (#1933 owns the verdict).
- The release lanes.

`contour.rs` was 446 lines before this PR (over the 400-line law). This PR adds 15 lines. A split is owed separately.

Changelog: 2D Contour refuses a picked ring whose side lies in the part at each level (Outside on a hole wall, Inside on a block outline), with the fix in the message. Before, it cut only the top plane and posted with no warning.

Effort: high

Fixes #1927

title: fix(2d): cut a stock open run one radius off by its side
body:
## What changed

A Contour on an open run that is picked on the stock no longer rides the run with the tool centre. The tool centre now stands one tool radius plus the stock to leave off the run, on the side that Side names:

- Outside: the side of the run without stock.
- Inside: the stock's side of the run.
- Auto: the side away from the part.

Files:

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_run_stock.rs` (new): `contour_open_run_sided`. It reads the stock and part sections at each cut level and offsets the run with the #1777 `offset_run`. It checks the ride against the part with `clear_of_part`. Climb keeps the stock on the right of the tool (#1555).
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_run_side.rs`: `material_side` takes the body name for its messages ("part" or "stock"). The part messages are not changed. Some helpers are now `pub(super)`.
- `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`: the Contour selection arm calls `contour_open_run_sided` for runs that are not part runs. It gives the raw Side, the stock facets and the setup's parts (`keep_parts`).
- `crates/app/src/operation/selection.rs`: the note "Side does not apply to open runs" shows only when no pick is on the stock.
- `docs/decisions/1928-stock-open-run-offset.md`: the decision.

Refused by name, never guessed:

- Inside or Outside when no stock is beside the run at a cut level.

Box stock with retained cut history now preserves machined walls and cavities through side-on quarter turns.
The carry retains swept-tool geometry and reads separate material intervals along the new columns.
Later cuts, stock clips, and further turns keep those intervals.
Fixture checks use the intervals on columns and between columns.
A fixture can contact a finished wall or occupy a cavity without a false collision.
The verdict still detects a later cut through the part.

The change starts from upstream/main `6f8b309d`.
Effort: max (not escalated).
No process files change.

## Cause

The old carry knew column heights but lost the wall position between column centres.
It extended a turned face to the next empty centre and filled cavities between the outer faces.
The pins reproduced a 6.5 mm wall instead of 6.2 mm.
The pocket floor became 6 mm instead of 2 mm.

Retry a machining mesh once at half the planning chord when its measured deviation exceeds the requested tolerance.

title: feat(wire-edm): per-ruling kerf widening and a stated verify tolerance for 4-axis cuts
body:
## What changed

A 4-axis Wire Contour had one widening for the whole cut: every ruling stood off the profiles as far as the worst twist needs. The straight stretches of a punch were then oversize. The wire verify also read a tessellated loft's facets as a gouge of a few microns, with no way to state the model's chord tolerance.

- **Motion** (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/ruled_widen.rs`): `WireWidening { PerRuling, Uniform }`. `PerRuling` is the default. Each ruling stands off by what its own twist needs. Transition rulings 1 mm from the ends of a long span end the widening near the twist. The existing ruled kerf law judges the emitted wire at every height. A path that fails it is refused by name.
- **Sim** (`crates/sim/src/verify/wire/`): `WireJob.verify_tol`. The kerf law lets a reading enter the facets by no more than the stated tolerance. The threading law and the slug law do not use it. A tolerance that is negative, not finite or not below the kerf offset is refused as unreadable. A gouge names the deepest reading at any height.
- **App**: the 4-axis block stores `widening` and `verify_tolerance` (0 to 0.25 mm at the operation door). The two values go through `EditOperationParams` and the project file. The widening is in the stamp digest. The post gate's report line states the tolerance and the deepest reading that it let pass. A 4-axis gouge with no stated tolerance adds a hint that names the model's chord tolerance.
- **UI**: the operation page shows "Stand off" and "Verify tolerance" in the 4-axis block.
- **Docs**: `site/content/guide/operations-edm.md`, `docs/decisions/1170-wire-ruling-kerf.md`.

There is no new command. The MCP surface takes the two keys through the operation parameters DTO (`four_axis.widening`, `four_axis.verify_tolerance`).

## Readings

Motion, square 10 to round 8, 64 points, twist tolerance 0.05 mm:

- Per ruling: the middle of each side stands as a plain taper of its lean (less than 0.003 mm more than the kerf offset). The rulings next to the corners stand 0.015 to 0.05 mm more.
- Uniform: every ruling stands 0.0207 mm more. The note says `the wire is held 0.1857 mm off both profiles`.
- A punch with one twisted flank: `9 of 13 rulings stand within 0.0001 mm of the kerf offset`.

App, square 8 lofted toward a circle, faceted at a chord tolerance of 0.0117 mm:

- No tolerance: `Punch1: wire gouge: the kerf of move 2 enters the part by 0.0004 mm near X-8.019 Y-0.833 at Z2.001 (64 move(s) gouge; the deepest reading at any height is 0.0112 mm) - a tessellated loft's facets stand past its ruled surface by up to the chord tolerance of the model: ...`
- Tolerance 0.0028: refused, `..., past the stated verify tolerance 0.0028 mm (40 move(s) gouge; the deepest reading at any height is 0.0112 mm)`.
- Tolerance 0.0117: posts. The report line says `kerf judged under the stated verify tolerance 0.0117 mm: the kerf enters the model's facets by at most 0.0112 mm, near X-7.468 Y-7.980 at Z6.000`.
- Tolerance 0.2: refused, `the verify tolerance 0.2 mm is not zero or a positive number below the kerf offset 0.1650 mm`.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-motion` lib, `wire_edm::ruled_widen_tests`: `a_square_to_round_punch_is_widened_only_where_it_twists`, `only_the_twisted_flank_of_a_punch_is_widened`, `a_twisted_flank_ends_its_widening_at_the_transition_rulings`.
- `camcraft-sim` lib, `verify::wire::tol_tests` (5 tests).
- `camcraft-app` `wire_verify_tol`: `a_tessellated_loft_posts_under_its_chord_tolerance_and_is_refused_below_it`, `the_widening_and_the_tolerance_are_stored_and_bounded_at_the_door`.
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `wire_four_axis_states_the_stand_off_choice_and_the_verify_tolerance`.

Quick gate on the final head `fc6848cf0`, all green. Rerun on the final head: `camcraft-motion` lib `wire_edm` (33 passed), `camcraft-motion` test `wire_fans` (7 passed), `camcraft-ui` lib `wire` (15 passed, includes the pinning test). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean. Results after the merge of main, from the worker: `camcraft-app` binaries `wire_verify_tol` (2), `wire_4axis` (8), `solid_law_goldens` (7) passed. Earlier results on the same app code: `camcraft-sim` lib `verify::wire` (20), `wire_fans` (2), `wire_stamp` (7), `golden_cl` (33), `project_roundtrip` (73), `wire_taper_angle`, `wire_contour`, `wire_post`, `wire_tabs`, `wire_burnout`, `wire_readers`, `edm_conditions`, `conformance`, `mcp_wire_contour`, `sodick_wire_post`. The clippy run of `camcraft-sim` and `camcraft-app` was clean earlier and was not run again.

## Screenshots

The operation page, Geometry tab, with the 4-axis block on. The images come from the test harness render. They are on the `screenshots` branch and are not part of this PR.

Before (main): the block ends with "Twist tolerance".

![Before](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/688073aeff311d345c75a109918bc3279d5cbb0f/pr-1921/before.png?raw=true)

`crates/app/tests/golden/wire_4axis_punch.cl` and `golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_4axis_punch.nc` are regenerated. The pose words moved by microns (for example `-8167` to `-8166`). 3. Minimum depth: settled. The post agrees. Q(dmin) clamps the cut of one pass below the pass before it.
4. Internal rounding of `dd * sqrt(n)`: open. No source states it. The post's guard stays.

The five Fanuc-family posts now write each length word with a decimal point: `Z14.`, never `Z14`. Fanuc parameter 3401 bit 0 (DPI) sets how the control reads a word with no point. With DPI=0 the control reads `Z14` as 0.014 mm, and a rapid to it goes almost to Z0. With the point, DPI=0 and DPI=1 read the same value.

- `assets/posts/fanuc.cps`, `haas.cps`, `mazak.cps`, `doosan-dnm.cps`: a new helper `pt` adds the point. The length format `fu` and the angle format `fa` use it. The helper `fn` keeps the old trimmed text for comments and for macro-B expressions (a macro-B constant is not scaled by DPI).
- `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`: the same for X (diameter), Z, I, K, R, the C angle, the feed per revolution and the thread lead (`F2.`), and the G76 R finish allowance. The G76 P/Q and G83 Q words stay in whole least increments: the control documents these addresses as "no decimal point".
- Feeds per minute are not changed (`F300`, or in/min at two decimals).
- `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`: a new law bullet "A length word carries its decimal point (#1836)".
- `docs/decisions/1836-fanuc-decimal-point.md`: the decision entry.

## The golden changes

All golden diffs of the Fanuc-family posts add only a trailing `.` to whole-number length, angle, lead and feed-per-rev words (for example `G00 X10 Y0 Z5` becomes `G00 X10. Y0. Z5.`). No value changes. No block is added or removed. The probe macro lines (`IF[ABS[#5063-25]GT0.001]...`, `#190=#100+17`) do not change. The goldens of the other posts do not change.

`crates/post/tests/explain_fanuc_family.rs` now writes its Explain golden when `WRITE_GOLDEN` is set, as the other golden tests do.

## Pinning tests

`crates/post/tests/decimal_point_fanuc_family.rs`:
- `the_mill_posts_write_a_whole_number_length_with_its_point` (fanuc, haas, mazak, doosan-dnm: `Z14.`, `Z-8.`, `X30.`, and no motion word with a bare length)
- `the_mill_posts_write_a_whole_number_inch_length_with_its_point` (the same four posts in inch: `Z1.`, `Z-1.`)
- `the_lathe_post_writes_a_whole_number_length_and_feed_per_rev_with_its_point` (fanuc-lathe: `X30. Z14.`, `Z-8.`, `F1.`)

The existing tests with inline G-code text of these posts now expect the point.

## Readings

- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: all test binaries pass, with the new `decimal_point_fanuc_family` tests.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app` on the touched binaries: all pass. The full app suite was also run one time. Only `sodick_alc400g` fails, and it fails on main too (#1856, the fix is on PR #1857).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- A script compared each changed golden with main: each diff only adds a `.` after a whole-number word.

## What was not exercised

- No real control was run with DPI=0 or DPI=1. The behaviour comes from the published parameter documentation.
- The feed-per-minute format and the non-Fanuc posts (Sinumerik, Heidenhain, Tormach, grblHAL, TinyG, Carvera) are not changed and not examined again.
- The release-tier heavy lanes and the pixel snapshots were not run.

Changelog: Fanuc, Haas, Mazak, Doosan DNM and Fanuc lathe posts now write each whole-number length, angle and feed-per-revolution word with a decimal point (`Z14.`), so that a control with parameter 3401#0 DPI=0 does not read it in least increments (#1836).

Effort: high

body:
Fork synced at v0.20.0 (process files at PROCESS_VERSION 71).

## What changed

The 2D Pocket can now cut only what a larger previous tool left. It uses the rest generator of #1446 (`machining2d::rest_pocket`).

- **Parameter.** `OpParams::Pocket` has a new optional `rest` group: previous tool diameter, its corner radius, the stock it left on the walls, and the rest allowance. `None` is off. Off is the default and the plain pocket.
- **Undoable edit.** You change the group through `EditOperationParams`. Undo and redo restore it.
- **Project file.** The key is `rest` (an object). A file without the key reads as off, so the file version does not change.
- **Stamp.** The stamp writes the group (byte `0xD7`) only when it is on. Each value of the group changes the stamp.
- **Generation.** When the group is on, generation calls `rest_pocket`. Its note ("rest machining trusts the entered previous tool ...") goes into the path notes.
- **Refusals by name, in the generator's own words, when you make, edit or retool the operation** (not only at Generate):
  - a previous tool that is not larger than the operation's tool (new `rest_gate`, run from `tool_gate` and from the edit);
  - a value that is negative or not finite, a previous tool diameter that is 0 or less, or a corner radius larger than the previous tool's radius;
  - the Zigzag or Adaptive strategy;
  - pre-drilled entry with rest machining on (`REST_PREDRILLED`). `rest_pocket` does not read the holes, and the program must not drop a user setting without saying so.
- **Motion crate.** `RestParams` has a new `validate_alone` (the checks that do not need a tool, plus "the previous tool diameter must be positive"). The strategy check moved into a public `rest_strategy`. Its text did not change.
- **MCP.** `edit_operation` sets the group (`"rest": null` turns it off). There is a new row in the camcraft-mcp skill. Area: mcp.
- **Not in this PR: the dialog group.** It is not part of "Done means", and it needs before/after screenshots and the UI gate. The page keeps the group as it is when you apply the page. Follow-up: #1815.

## How tested

The new pinning tests are in `crates/app/tests/rest_pocket.rs`:
- `the_rest_pass_cuts_only_the_corners_posts_and_matches_its_golden`: the fixture is a 60 x 40 pocket with 3 mm corners. A 12 mm end mill roughs it, then a 4 mm end mill does the rest pass. The golden is `pocket_rest_corners.cl`. All cuts stay in the corners. The program posts and the verification report is clean.
- `read_against_the_simulated_roughing_pass`: the roughing pass is simulated first on the stock dexel grid. Then:
  - no rapid of the rest pass hits stock;
  - every plunge goes down on floor that is already clear, and its rim touches stock for no more than one level;
  - all 8 rings (4 corners x 2 levels) cut stock, and air is less than half of each ring.
- `the_group_is_an_undoable_edit_and_the_project_file_keeps_it`
- `a_previous_tool_that_is_not_larger_is_refused_by_name_at_the_edit_and_the_retool` (edit, create and retool)
- `values_and_strategies_the_rest_pass_cannot_run_are_refused_by_name`
- `mcp_sets_refuses_undoes_and_saves_the_group` (set, refuse, save, reopen, null, undo)

Other tests:
- `operation::rest_op_tests::the_rest_group_moves_the_stamp`
- `crates/motion/tests/rest2d.rs`: a new case for a 0 mm previous tool.

Mutation check: I deleted each new refusal line, the stamp line and the generation line one at a time, ran the test that pins it, and saw it fail. Then I restored the file and compared it with a backup. All 11 failed when deleted and were restored byte for byte: the motion "must be positive" check, rest_op's three refusals, sane's `named_refusal` and `is_sane` lines, `rest_gate` in `tool_gate`, `rest_gate` in the edit, the refusal arm inside `rest_gate`, the `0xD7` stamp block, and the `rest_pocket` call in generation.

The existing pocket goldens do not change (`golden_cl`, `adaptive_trochoid`, `roughing2d` and the others in the list above).

## What I did not test

- I did not run the program on a machine, and I did not take screenshots (there is no UI change).

title: feat(sim): sinker body electrode - outline atom, tool record and electrode from faces
body:
fork synced at v0.20.0 · process files at PROCESS_VERSION 71 · branch from `upstream/main` 03dc12c6

## What changed

A sinker electrode can now be a BODY: a closed outline extruded along Z. Before this PR the stock sim burned a rectangular face only (the box atom of #541), and `electrode_from_faces` refused each cavity that was not an axis-aligned rectangle (`NON_RECTANGULAR`, which named this issue).

1. **Sim atom** (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/dexel_outline.rs`, `stock_sim::simulate_outline`). The outline, grown by the spark gap, is swept along straight chords through the column grid. The result is exact at each column centre: nothing is sampled. The grown section is the inside of the polygon joined with a stadium on each edge. A chord meets a stadium in one interval, in closed form. The face height is linear along the chord, so the lowest height is at the first or the last covered parameter. An arc, a posed move, a non-finite move, a bad gap and an outline that is no section are refused by name before a column is lowered. The box atom is not changed.
2. **Tool record** (`Tool::outline`, `crates/tools/src/electrode_outline.rs`). Points in mm about the burn point; empty for a rectangular face. `diameter` and `width` stay the X and Y extents of the outline, and the outline is centred on the burn point. The record's door (`is_sane`, `torch_refusal`) refuses by name an outline that is no simple section (3 to 1024 points) and sizes that do not agree with it. The key `outline` goes through the project file, the library file, the tools crate's catalog reader and the MCP `add_tool` / `edit_tool` definitions (additive, written only when stated). The operation stamp digests the points.
3. **`electrode_from_faces`** (`crates/motion/src/sinker_electrode_body.rs`). A cavity that is no axis-aligned rectangle yields a body electrode. The obstruction check uses the cavity's own outline as the column. The size law of #543 judges an outline on its extents (`Undersize::outline`).
4. **The program verdict** burns a record that has an outline with the outline atom, and a record without one with the box atom. The field eye still refuses a program with an electrode (#548).

The decisions are in `docs/decisions/1152-electrode-body.md`.

## Done means

- A rounded-corner pocket's faces yield an electrode whose burn `simulate_document` judges clean: `a_rounded_pockets_faces_yield_an_electrode_whose_burn_is_judged_clean`.
- A burn of the same electrode in a smaller cavity is convicted as a gouge: `the_same_electrode_in_a_smaller_cavity_is_convicted_as_a_gouge`.
- The non-rectangular refusal of #547 is gone: `a_cavity_that_is_no_rectangle_yields_a_body_electrode` (a rotated rectangle, an L, a chamfered corner).

## How tested

Pinning tests:

- `crates/sim/tests/stock_outline.rs` (new, 5 tests): a plunge burns the section grown by the gap and nothing else; a rectangular outline burns what the box atom burns; a sampled oracle with an independent distance rule and inside rule bounds a sloping sweep from both sides; each refusal is by name and leaves the grid untouched; garbage input burns or refuses and never raises a column.
- `crates/tools/src/electrode_outline.rs` (2 unit tests), `crates/tools/src/catalog_asset_tests.rs::a_catalog_electrode_keeps_its_outline`.
- `crates/motion/src/sinker_electrode_body_tests.rs` (new, 4 tests), `sinker_electrode_tests.rs` (`a_cavity_that_is_no_rectangle_yields_a_body_electrode`, `a_body_electrodes_column_is_the_cavitys_outline_not_its_bounds`), `sinker_undersize.rs::sinker_undersize_judges_an_outline_on_its_extents`. The existing electrode fuzz test now also derives body electrodes.
- `crates/app/tests/sinker_electrode_body.rs` (new, 5 tests): the two "Done means" tests; an L cavity; a diamond cavity; the project file round trip and the stale burn after a re-cut outline. Each clean verdict has a contrast: the rectangle of the same two sizes is convicted in the pocket's corners (rounded pocket) and in the notch (L).
- `crates/app/tests/sinker_electrode_mcp.rs::a_rounded_pocket_yields_a_body_electrode_over_mcp`, `crates/app/tests/tool_library.rs::a_body_electrodes_outline_roundtrips_through_the_library`, `crates/app/src/stock_sim_held_tests.rs::the_outline_atom_burns_a_column_grid_and_a_field_refuses_it_by_name`.

Mutation check: 51 mutations, one for each new refusal line, stamp line and dispatch line. Each mutation was applied, the pinning suite was run and was red, the file was restored and compared byte for byte with its backup. 51 of 51 red.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`, 5 steps. The first run: tools, sim, motion and app suites green (21 min), the ui step red with a compile error (the tool page's draft built a `Tool` without the new field). The fix makes the draft carry the outline (`ToolUi::outline`), pinned by `crates/ui/tests/sinker_setup.rs::the_tool_draft_carries_a_body_electrodes_outline_through_an_apply`. The ui step was then run again with `--only ui` (10 suites): green. Only `crates/ui` changed between the two runs. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`: clean. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## What was not exercised

- A real EDM control. The conditions are synthetic and the blocks are built in code.
- An orbit or a side burn of a body electrode through an operation. The lateral sweep of the atom is pinned in the sim crate against the oracle.
- The UI pages. No page generates, shows or edits an outline (#548 owns the sinker pages). The tool page's draft carries the outline through an Apply (pinned); an edit of the X or Y size of a body electrode on the page is refused by name by the record's door.
- The batch gate, the release lanes and the pixel snapshots.
- Windows and macOS.

## Limits, each refused by name or filed

- A wall picked as its welded (curved) face: refused as before. #1808.
- A drafted wall or a stepped floor: refused as before. #1809.
- A finish pass of a cavity with sharp corners that are not square to the axes: the size law refuses it as under size. #1810.
- An outline of more than 1024 points: refused by name.
- An older build reads a body electrode as the rectangle of its two sizes (it skips the unknown key). That rectangle contains the outline, so the old build burns more, not less.

No new command, so no new MCP tool. `electrode_from_faces` answers `electrode.shape` and `electrode.outline`. The camcraft-mcp skill's table is a process file and is not touched here.

Changelog: A sinker electrode can be a body: `electrode_from_faces` makes an outline electrode for a cavity that is not an axis-aligned rectangle (a rounded-corner pocket, an L, a rotated rectangle), the tool record carries the outline through the project file, the library and MCP, and the program verdict burns it with a new outline atom.

title: feat(sim): carry machined stock into a setup turned side-on
body:
## What changed

A setup that stands the part on its edge can now take "What Setup1 leaves behind" as its stock. The turn is a quarter turn about X or Y from the setup before it. Before this change the carry was refused by name (`CARRY_TURN_REFUSAL`).

**camcraft-sim** (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/carry_side.rs`, new):

- `SideTurn` is one of the sixteen side-on quarter turns. `CarryTurn` is a lattice turn or a side turn.
- `Body::carry_side` reads the column body again along the new tool axis:
  - The level axis that stays level is re-indexed, centre onto centre.
  - The old heights become slabs of one cell, centred on the old Z range. A face inside a slab counts the slab whole.
  - The old level axis becomes the height. The top and the floor are the hull of the old column centres that hold material. Each end moves out to the next centre that holds no material, or to the lattice edge. A cavity between the ends is filled.
- The carried body is never smaller than the body the columns hold. It is at most one grid cell larger on a turned face. The raw faces of a box stock at the lattice edge are read exactly.
- The field engine refuses a side-on turn by name (`FIELD_SIDE_CARRY_REFUSAL`). The shipped engine is the column engine.
- `CARRY_TURN_REFUSAL` has shorter words: "the stock simulation carries machined stock only through quarter turns (steps of 90° about X, Y or Z)". A turn off the quarter is still refused and the app still names the turn and the two setups.

**camcraft-app**:

- `stock_sim_carry.rs`: `carry_turn` returns a `CarryTurn`. The program walk judges the body before a side-on turn and keeps those gouges for the final verdict. The hull can hide a gouge that an earlier setup cut. This is the same fold that a block left for a new block gets (#320).
- `side_on_note` adds a note line to the gate: the stock was turned side-on, and what the verdict reads.
- `rest/across.rs` and `rest.rs` hold a `CarryTurn`. The rest reading, the judged stock, the prior plan and the carried block follow the same turn. The `Debug` text of a lattice turn is unchanged, so no shipped stamp moves.

No user-facing command is new. No MCP tool is owed.

title: fix(post): refuse unsupported Sodick angle-word moves
body:
## What changed

Keep Sodick constant taper refused until its mapping preserves the generated wire path.
Refuse WireAngle records by operation name even when the section omits WireTaper.
Stop cutting that section instead of silently writing a vertical move.
Record the evidence and rejected mappings in docs/decisions/1496-sodick-taper.md.
This uses the issue's allowed outcome of documenting the mapping limits and retaining refusal.

## Cause

The post ignored WireAngle records.
A direct angle-word stream without WireTaper could therefore emit a vertical cut without a warning.
Lower-guide XY and explicit upper-guide offsets cannot simply become nominal A angles without proving the corner and transition motion.
The alternative angle stream uses work-relative WirePlane, which does not establish Sodick's table-relative program height.

Sodick's [2012 LN1W/LN2W training manual](https://fab.cba.mit.edu/content/tools/sodick_edm/sodick_user_manual_small.pdf), printed pages 66-70, describes G51/G52, A, G50 and the table/guide settings.
That newer-control source does not prove the complete mapping for this post's Mark 21/EX21 target.
Unconfirmed items are Mark 21/EX21 TP/TN initialization and datum/calibration correspondence, corner and lead/cancel interpolation, and the signed angle mapping in that frame.
No unconfirmed words are emitted.

## Tests

`sodick_refuses_angle_words_even_without_section_taper` fails on the original post and passes with the guard.
It covers positive, negative and zero angles.
`sodick_vertical_stream_still_posts_without_angle_words` preserves vertical posting.

title: fix(3d): a whole-model 3D Pocket clears an open-sided notch past its edge
body:
## What changed

A whole-model 3D Pocket used the model's silhouette as its footprint, and the level law erodes that by the tool radius. So the cutter's edge never passed the silhouette. On a notch open to the part's outside, the pocket left a band one radius wide along the open edges at the full stock height, and the op reported `ok` (#1749).

- `camcraft-motion`: new `machining3d::open_sides` (`machining3d/open_side.rs`). It grows the silhouette by the tool radius less 0.01 mm, minus a keep-out region. Where a level is open, the cutter centre now goes up to the silhouette edge. Where a level's material stands flush with the silhouette, the band is narrower than the erosion, so it cuts nothing there and a plain block gets no new ring.
- `camcraft-app`: the new `operation/open_side.rs` applies this footprint in the Pocket3D arm and in the Multi-Axis Rough arm (the stamped twin: one ladder). It applies only to the source-built footprint of an untilted whole-model source. A picked or Boundary-controlled region, and a tilted plane, stay as before. The keep-out is the silhouette of the setup's other parts.
- `keep_law::kept_models`: the setup's other parts now go into the solid law for Pocket3D and Multi-Axis Rough as a second net. This net also reports a cut through a second part that stands inside the model's own silhouette. Before, that cut read `ok` (the ladder's islands come only from its own model).
- `shared_face_bodies`: the #1706 pin (`the_sample_as_imported_refuses_the_3d_pocket_by_name`) pinned the old law. No 6 mm tool fit inside the 6.53 mm strip, so the op refused. Under the new law the pocket clears the stock beside the strip with no gouge. The pin is renamed to `the_sample_as_imported_roughs_the_3d_pocket_beside_its_silhouette`. Recorded in `docs/decisions/1749-pocket3d-open-side.md`.
  - The sample op does NOT post with the job's tool (takeover commit 82c9f082b). `EM-0600-4FL` has 15 mm of flute and an 8 mm shank; the part is 118 mm tall. Verify names `shank_hit` (part) and `rapid_in_stock` (the lifts out of those cuts), all `blocks_post`, and holds the post by R1. The test now deletes S1 (so the program gate runs) and asserts this reading by name: status `ok`, gate ran and passed, no gouge, only these two kinds, all on R1, `ok: false`, `held_by: [R1]`. Then it gives the tool 125 mm flutes and a 6 mm shank, generates again, and asserts a clean verify.
  - Cause: the 3D Pocket ladder keeps only the flute radius off the material above a level. The same R1 moves with full-depth flutes give no findings. A closed cavity with no open side gives the same kinds with main's footprint law and with this PR's law. So the shank blindness is on main; this PR only gives the sample a path. It is owed in #1844 (P3).

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_open_side.rs`. The fixture is built in code: a 30 mm block with its +X+Y quadrant notched down to Z 20, in a stock that fits it in XY with its top at Z 32. The tool is a 10 mm flat end mill, with offset rings and shell on.
- `an_open_sided_notch_is_cleared_to_the_parts_edge`: measures the stock the path leaves (the lowest flat-end disc over each column) along both open edges, 0.05 mm inside the part edge. It must be at the floor, Z 20. It also checks that no feed disc enters the part's material at its Z, and that verify is clean. Before the fix, the stock stayed at Z 32.000 at (14.95, 10.80).
- `an_open_side_never_reaches_into_a_neighbouring_part`: a second part 1 mm past the +X open edge. No feed disc comes within R of it, verify is clean, and the +Y open edge is still cleared.
- `a_part_standing_in_the_notch_is_named_by_the_solid_law`: a second part on the notch floor, inside the model's silhouette, is reported (warnings > 0), not read as `ok`.

Mutation checks. Each mutation was reverted afterwards and the file compared byte-for-byte with its backup:
- `open_footprint` returns the region unchanged: the open-edge test fails (stock at Z 32.000).
- Keep-out made empty: the neighbour test fails (81 solid-law warnings; the second net fires).
- The `keep_law` line removed: the neighbour test and the solid-law test both fail.

Gates (Linux):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the Pocket3D-only version of the change: motion suites ok. App suites ok except `operations::multiaxis_rough_peels_the_same_ladder_and_poses_its_walls` (150 vs 134 moves). That failure led to the Multi-Axis Rough change. The #1706 pin also failed there; it is updated as described above.
- After the final change, these targeted app suites, all green: operations, level_links, ribbon, suppressed_rest, rest_across_setups, stock_engine_agreement, setup_align, probe_op, remachining, drill_prior, area_controls, project_roundtrip, pocket3d_hsm, shared_face_bodies, keep_law, neighbour_law, kept_parts_live, coarse_laws, center_cut_multiaxis, pocket3d_open_side.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The takeover commit changes only the sample test and the decision file. Its quick gate (`--base 02892e348`) selects only that test.
- `generate.rs` stays at 3668 lines (this PR adds 11). Its split is owed and is not done here.
- Fixtures (vise jaws) are not subtracted from the open-side band. The decision file says so. The fixture laws of verify still judge them.
- The tilted (3+2) case is owed in #1774 (PR #1780, stacked on this PR).

- The full quick gate was not re-run on the final head; only the targeted suites listed above were. The motion crate did not change after the quick gate's green motion run.
- No batch gate, heavy lanes, ui suites (`crates/ui/tests/operations.rs` uses Pocket3D) or snapshots.
- A tilted (3+2) 3D Pocket keeps the old silhouette law, so it can still leave the ridge.
- Stock that reaches more than about two radii past the silhouette is still not cleared by a whole-model 3D Pocket. That would be the stock-outline reading the 2D pocket has had since #12, which is a larger change. See the decision file.

Changelog: A whole-model 3D Pocket (and Multi-Axis Rough) clears a notch open to the part's outside past its open edge instead of leaving a tool-radius ridge, keeps off the setup's other parts, and warns when it cuts through one.

Effort: high (no escalation)

title: fix(boundary): edges bound the cut in any pick mode, two edges keep the area between them
body:
## What changed

- **Edge picks reach the Boundary group in any pick mode** (`crates/ui/src/feature_click.rs`). An armed boundary row took the toolbar's pick kinds, so in Faces mode (the usual one) a click on an edge picked the face, and no edge could bound the cut. It now takes faces and edges whatever the mode. Points stay refused by name, as before.
- **Two or more separate edges bound the area between them** (`crates/geometry/src/boundary_chains.rs`, new; one arm in `boundary::resolve`). The open boundary may hold separate open chains. Each chain splits the stock the way a single chain does (`sides_of_chain`). Each keeps the side that holds the operation's own area, and the area kept is the area between the chains. A face bounded by two of its edges is faced between them, and the rows run on past the face at the open ends. Face lays its rows along the first chain. Side B keeps everything beyond the chains.
- **Refused by name, never guessed** (each pinned and mutation-checked, below):
  - chains that touch or cross ("chains i and j touch or cross");
  - a chain with the operation's area evenly on both sides;
  - a Contour given two chains ("a Contour rides one open chain");
  - an include / exclude made of separate chains: the Apply door, as for one open chain (`PickShape::is_open` covers the new `PickShape::Chains`).
- The old refusal "the boundary picks spell N separate open runs" is gone. The maintainer asked for exactly that case to work. The `area_picks.rs` assertion that pinned it now pins two chains.
- Everything is a command: the picks go into the page draft, and Apply commits them as the existing undoable `EditOperationParams::with_area`. Over MCP, `set_operation_area`'s `open.picks` takes edge chain ids. It already accepted them; a test now pins it. title: fix(tools): assemble modular multi-piece tool bodies (#361)
body:
## What changed

`ToolBody` now stores an ordered `pieces: Vec<BodyPiece>` table while keeping `facets` and `frame` as the merged body. Each piece records its label, facet count, rigid placement, and transformed STEP coordinate systems (`BodyCsys`).

`tool_body_assembly` and `tool_body_mate` load piece files, mate child `MCS` frames onto parent `CSW*` frames (or explicit named parent and child frames), enforce the facet budget, and rebuild merged facets cleanly. Ambiguous, missing, mismatched, or single-piece-removal inputs fail with named error messages.

`SetToolBody::attach_piece`, `SetToolBody::attach_loaded_piece`, and `SetToolBody::remove_piece` update modular assemblies in one undoable command step. `ToolBodyDto` serializes `pieces` additively and omits the key for single-piece bodies without CSYS metadata.

MCP tools `attach_tool_body_piece` and `remove_tool_body_piece`, `get_tool_body` (`pieces`), and the Tool Editor Modular Assembly section expose piece attachment and removal to agents and users.

## Cause

Single-piece tool body replacement discarded prior pieces when a user attached a clamping unit, extension, or modular lathe head from vendor STEP/STL/OBJ files. No CSYS mating or piece tracking existed to align multi-piece assemblies or judge them together in simulation.

## Tests

title: feat(wcs): store WCS axis flips (Flip X/Y/Z); refuse post and generation by name
body:
Stacked on #1717 (base `issue/1648-wcs-page-work-offset`). Retarget this PR to `main` before #1717 merges.

## What changed

Part 1 of issue 1649 ("Split in two"): the WCS page can store a flipped axis. This PR does not change posted G-code.

- **Stored flags.** A new component `schema::WcsFlip([bool; 3])` is on the setup's WCS entity. "No flip" is stored as no component.
- **One undoable command.** `SetWcsFlip::for_setup` sets the flags of a setup's WCS. It refuses an unknown setup by name. If the WCS was never placed, it places it at the identity, and undo removes it again.
- **WCS page.** Three toggles, "Flip X", "Flip Y" and "Flip Z", are under the quarter turns. A lit toggle is a flipped axis. When an axis is flipped, a note tells the user that posting and generating are refused until the flip is cleared.
- **Viewport triad.** A flipped axis is drawn in the opposite direction. A flipped WCS at the origin does not hide the world axes.
- **Refusal by name.** The post verification gate and the generation door (`collect_job`) refuse a flipped WCS. An example message: "the WCS (G54) has its X axis flipped; posting or generating with a flipped WCS is not available yet - clear the flip on the WCS page (operations: Face1)". All post paths use the gate, so no path posts with a flip set.
- **Project file v62.** A WCS row can have the optional key `flip` (`{"x": true}`), and only flipped axes are written. A file without the key opens with no flip. A `flip` key on a row that is not a WCS is refused as corrupt.
- **Undo keeps the flip.** `DeleteEntity`, `DeleteSetup` and the datum transfer of `CreateSetup` keep the flip.
- **MCP.** A new tool, `set_wcs_flip {x?, y?, z?, setup?}`. An axis that is not given keeps its flag. `get_job` shows `setups[].wcs.flip`. The camcraft-mcp skill has the tool row and a "Shipped" line.
- **Decisions.** `docs/decisions/1720-wcs-flip-flags.md`.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/wcs_flip.rs` (new, 10 tests). It pins these points:
  - the command, undo and redo;
  - the refusal of an unknown setup;
  - the post refusal by name, and the same stream after the flip is cleared;
  - the generation refusal by name;
  - the setup name in the message;
  - DeleteSetup and DeleteEntity undo;
  - the datum transfer;
  - the project round trip, an old file, and a corrupt row;
  - the MCP tool and `get_job`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_flip_tests.rs` (new, 3 tests). It pins the toggle layout and live state, the click to the command, the reversed triad, undo and redo, and the status line.
- The existing suites `wcs_page_tests`, `wcs_gizmo_tests` and `wcs_circle_tests` pass.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/1648-wcs-page-work-offset`: the app step (302 suites) passed in 1279 s. A file that I wrote into the worktree during the run made the gate VOID before its ui step. Then I ran the same ui step command by hand on the same tree, and it passed (lib 778 tests and 12 suites).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- No before/after screenshots: this worker cannot start the GUI. The maintainer must add them before `/merge-ready` offers the PR.
- Posting with a flip (part 2 of issue 1649) is not in this PR. There are no NC golden changes.
- No script verb. The decision file gives the reason.

title: fix(post): grblHAL, Carvera and TinyG write no motion after the no-plane refusal
body:
## What changed

`grblhal.cps`, `carvera.cps` and `tinyg.cps`: `xyFirst` now returns `false` when it refuses the first X/Y traverse because the stream states no ClearancePlane and no RetractPlane. Its callers write nothing for that move: `onRapid`, `onLinear`/`onCircular` (through `startXY`), and grblHAL's `onCycle`. X/Y stay unknown, so every later move of the section is refused the same way. The message is still given once per program. This is the rule the Tormach (#1614) and Fanuc-family (#1633) posts already follow.

Before this change, the refused rapid was still written as `G0 X20 Y10 Z2`, followed by the feeds. The app blocks the post on the warning, but the `post` CLI writes the file anyway, so the refused move ended up in the program text.

**TinyG too.** The issue says TinyG already stops through `startXY`. Its `onRapid` still wrote the combined rapid after the refusal, though, and the issue's "Done means" pin covers TinyG, so TinyG's `onRapid` gets the same guard. The decision is recorded in `docs/decisions/1682-refused-traverse-writes-nothing.md`.

## Pinning tests (`crates/post/tests/first_traverse_clearance.rs`)

- `a_first_traverse_with_no_stated_plane_is_refused_by_name`: now also asserts that no motion line carries an X or Y word, for grblHAL, TinyG and Carvera. It was red on the old scripts (grblHAL output: `G0 X20 Y10 Z2`, `G1 X20 Y10 Z-1 F500`, ...).
- `no_xy_motion_follows_the_refusal_whatever_the_first_move` (new): the first move of the section is a feed, an arc or a canned cycle. For each case it checks that the refusal is given by name and that no X/Y word is written.

**Mutation check.** I reverted each new guard line on its own, ran the suite, restored the file from a backup, touched it and compared it with `cmp`. Every mutation turned the suite red:

| post | line mutated | result |
|---|---|---|
| grblhal / carvera / tinyg | `onRapid` guard dropped | 1 failed |
| grblhal / carvera / tinyg | `xyFirst` refusal returns `true` | 2 failed |
| grblhal / carvera / tinyg | `startXY` refusal check dropped | 2 failed |
| grblhal / carvera | `onLinear` guard dropped | 2 failed |
| grblhal / carvera | `onCircular` guard dropped | 1 failed |
| grblhal | `onCycle` guard dropped | 1 failed |

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green. It ran 17 post suites (7 s) and 21 app suites, including `grblhal_post`, `carvera_post`, `tinyg_post` and `conformance` (97 s).

- The batch gate was not run, to keep within the budget.
- The Windows arms were not run.
- The app's posting path was not run end to end. It already blocks on the warning.

Changelog: grblHAL, Carvera and TinyG posts write no motion after refusing a first X/Y traverse with no stated clearance or retract plane (the `post` CLI no longer puts the refused move in the file)

title: fix(import): load a STEP closed shell that meshes open as an incomplete model
body:
## What changed

A STEP closed shell that meshes open (a real gap, e.g. walls missing on a face truck cannot mesh) used to be refused at import (#1576), so the part could not even be loaded for viewing or setup. Now the model import lands it **incomplete**:

- `step_closed::judge` returns the hole, named, instead of refusing; `step::parse_open` and `import::{load,parse}_model_open_within` keep it in `Graded::open`. Every other loader (`load_model`, `parse_model`, `*_graded_within`: fixtures-by-path, tool bodies) still refuses with the same words as before.
- `ImportModel` (GUI, MCP `import_model`, script `import`) lands the mesh with the fidelity-unknown sentinel (`model_fidelity::UNKNOWN_MM`, #1056) and the hole in a new component `schema::MeshOpen`. The sentinel rides every chord path (stock copies, setup clones, undo, save), so every operation on the model and the program verdict are refused at the post by the existing gate, and the program sim gives no verdict.
- New module `mesh_open`: the refusal words ("model 'X' was imported incomplete - closed shell #N (F faces) meshes open: ... - so it has walls missing and no gouge check against it can be trusted; re-export the model, or import an STL"), the model page / import status line ("Incomplete: ..."), and the MCP/script `reduced_fidelity` facts (`incomplete: true`, `hole`).
- The hole is traded by `UpdateModel` (new `with_hole`, undo restores it; a whole re-import clears it), `DeleteEntity` undo, and the project file (optional entity key `mesh_open`, written only beside `fidelity_unknown`; a `mesh_open` without the mark is refused as corrupt). No project version bump: an old reader drops the key and keeps the mark, so it still refuses (decision file).
- `model_fidelity::set` clears any hole, so a stale hole never speaks for a whole mesh.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/1610-open-shell-incomplete.md`.

## How tested

Pinning tests, new suite `crates/app/tests/import_step_open_shell.rs`:
- `a_closed_shell_that_meshes_open_imports_incomplete_with_its_hole_named` (the bent `fillet_corner.step` fixture: loads, facets present, hole named incl. the dropped face, summary/facts say incomplete; the graded loader still refuses)
- `every_operation_on_an_incomplete_model_is_refused_at_the_post_naming_the_hole` (verification report, sim not judged, `post_setup` refused, not the pre-v59 note)
- `the_hole_rides_undo_and_a_whole_reimport_clears_it`
- `the_hole_rides_the_project_file_and_is_refused_without_its_mark`

Updated: `step_seams_tests::the_importer_closes_seams_within_two_chord_tolerances_only` (the gap is now returned named, not refused, by `judge`).

title: fix(post): Tormach lathe moves one axis at a time after G30 and leaves the stock before it
body:
## What changed

`assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps` only. The mill post `tormach.cps` does not change.

LinuxCNC's G30 moves every axis in one straight line to the stored position (params 5181-5189). The operator stores that position, so the post cannot know where the line goes. Before this change, the first rapid after `G30` went diagonally to the start point, and the closing `G30` went diagonally from the last retract. Now:

- **After G30** (tool change, or a "home" after-operation), the first point is approached one axis at a time:
  - The point is outside the stock's diameter (all turning and threading starts): `G0 X`, then `G0 Z`.
  - The point is inside the diameter, in front of the face (a hole on centre): `G0 Z`, then `G0 X`. A point ON the face goes to the section's `ClearancePlane` first, then X, then Z down to the point.
  - Any other point: refused by name.
- **Before G30** (tool change, "home", program end): `G0 X` out to the stock's diameter, then `G0 Z` out to the face (or to the `ClearancePlane` when the corner is not clear in either axis). The lines go before the next section's notes and work offset word, because they are in the old frame.
- **Stock and planes** come from the stream's own `StockXY*`, `StockZTop` and `ClearancePlane` PARAMs. No margin is added by the post.
- **Refused by name:** no stock box; a first point inside the stock with no `ClearancePlane` in front of the face; a section that ends inside the stock's envelope; a section that ends on the stock's corner with no `ClearancePlane`; a feed, arc or thread half-turn as the first motion after G30.

**Order chosen:** X first, then Z, for every point outside the stock's diameter. For a hole on centre, X first from a G30 beside the bar moves into the bar, and a clearance diameter is not stated in the stream. Z first to the stated `ClearancePlane` needs no guess, so the post uses it there. The reasons are in `docs/decisions/1604-lathe-g30-rapid.md`.

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/lathe_post_tormach_g30.rs` (each pin mutation-checked; seven mutations of the post, each one fails at least one pin):

- `the_first_move_after_g30_is_x_alone_then_z_alone`: turning and G76 threading programs go `G0 X..` then `G0 Z..` after each G30; the hole goes `G0 Z30`, `G0 X0`, `G0 Z20`.
- `the_departure_goes_plus_x_then_plus_z_before_g30`: the hole ends `G0 X20` before G30; a section behind the face leaves `G0 Z10` before the next tool change, before the next work offset word.
- `no_stored_g30_outside_the_stock_is_reached_across_it`: for a 41 x 41 grid of stored G30 positions outside the stock, no G30 line and no added rapid crosses the stock (turning, hole and thread programs). The first move from every G30 is one axis, and every G30 line starts at the stock's outer corner.
- `a_missing_stock_or_clearance_is_refused_by_name`: no stock, no clearance plane in front of the face, an end on the corner with no clearance, an end inside the envelope, and a feed first after G30.

Mutations: radial approach Z-then-X; the old diagonal approach; no departure; departure without +Z; departure without +X; no clearance refusal; no stock refusal.

**Goldens:** the eight `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/*.nc` and the recorded `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/tormach-lathe/tool_change.nc` were regenerated. A script checked each diff: the first two-axis `G0` after each `G30` becomes one-axis `G0` lines that end at the same point; the lines added before a `G30` are one-axis `+X` or `+Z` moves; every other line is the same and in the same order. Result: GOLDEN DIFF OK (12 approaches split, 5 departures added). I also mutated a golden two ways (a changed F word, a changed end point) and the script failed both.

Hand-built test streams in `lathe_post_tormach`, `lathe_post_tormach_thread` and `lathe_cycle_exit` now state a stock (`tormach_lathe_support::stock_params`), because the post refuses a stream with no stock. Two assertions changed to the split approach (`G0 X12.1\nG0 Z14`), and the G76 drive-line test reads the last X before the G76 block.

Gates on head `9acdd7e8`: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green (post suites ok 24 s, app suites ok 1188 s, 0 failed; the changed recorded golden pulls in every post and app suite). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- **No PathPilot lathe Hub run was done.** A PathPilot lathe Hub run of the turning, thread and hole programs is wanted, with G30 stored (a) on centre in front of the face and (b) beside the bar behind the face.
- A box stock turned on a lathe: the post uses the box's largest half-width, not its half-diagonal, because the stream does not say if the stock is round. Filed as #1666 (P3).
- The idle tools of a gang plate: the post knows only the active tool's control point.

## Notes

- Open drafts #517, #518 and #468 also change `tormach-lathe.cps` in its G76 sections. This PR touches only one line there (the G76 drive-line rapid goes through the new approach after G30). Whichever PR merges second refreshes from main.
- Fork synced at v0.18.0 (process files at upstream PROCESS_VERSION); this branch is from `upstream/main`.

body:
#1198 slice (b): move handles with drag-to-move. Slice (a), the bottom bar, merged in #1203.

**GUI hand check needed.** The handles, the drag feel and the readout were tested only through the kittest harness and headless state tests. Nobody has looked at them on screen yet.

## What changed
- **Move mode in the bottom bar.** A seventh bar button (a four-armed cross) turns `State::move_handles` on and off. It is off by default, it is view state like pick-through, and it queues no command.
- **Handles** (`crates/ui/src/move_drag.rs`, painted by `crates/ui/src/egui_app/move_handles.rs`). With Move on and exactly one shown part selected, three arms in the axis colours start at the part's bounding-box centre and each ends in a ball. The arms stay 70 px long on screen at any zoom. The ball under the pointer is drawn larger.
- **Drag.** Pressing a ball takes the press before orbit and pick. Empty space still orbits. While the button is down, the preview slides the body along the axis (`world.rs` draws it offset) and never writes the world. The signed distance shows just above the bar. The distance is where the cursor ray comes closest to the axis line, so the part stays under the cursor in perspective and in ortho.
- **One command per drag.** The release queues `CommandKind::MoveModelBy { name, delta }`. The drain (`crates/ui/src/state_move_by.rs`) runs it as the Model page's own `MoveModel::new`, with the rotation copied bit for bit. - **What adds no history step:** Escape during a drag (the key is consumed), a drag that ends where it began, and turning Move off.
- **Turned setups.** When the active setup holds the part turned (#326), the drag happens in that setup's frame. The shown delta is rotated back into the document frame, so the part moves along the axis the user sees.

No new app command, so no new MCP tool. `MoveModelBy` is a UI queue verb over the existing `MoveModel`, and the MCP `move_model` tool already places a part through `MoveModel`. An agent can make every move a drag makes.

title: feat(edm): wire taper by angle word - the control's corner rule as machine data
body:
fork synced at v0.19.0.

## What changed

A wire EDM can now state an **angle-word taper dialect** in place of U/V moves. The control's behaviour goes in the machine file as data, so the verify can judge the lean the control will actually cut.

- **Machine data** (`post::machine::edm_taper`, new): `edm.taper_angle { positive: top_left|top_right, corner: mitre|cone }`. Both values are enumerated words with no default. A garbled word refuses the file. An unstated one is refused by name at generation. The angle code is `edm.codes.taper_angle`, a template with `{angle}`.
- **Generator** (`motion::wire_edm::taper`): a `WireCorner` rule.
  - `Mitre` is #536's path. On the fixture its CL equals #536's golden byte for byte (pinned).
  - `Cone` pivots the wire about each top-plane corner and holds the lean at the angle. The lower end runs on an arc of radius `H tan a`, laid as posed moves at most 2 degrees apart.
  - Under `cone`, a lead-in that meets a corner is refused by name.
- **Door** (`app::operation::wire_op::corner_rule`): a U/V machine keeps the mitre. An angle-word machine uses its stated rule. An incomplete rule is refused by name, and so is a 4-axis cut, because one angle cannot state two profiles. The rule is stamped only for angle-word machines, so U/V stamps do not change.
- **Post** (`app::posting_wire::angled`, `wire-iso.cps`):
  - Each move's X Y is written on the programmed plane, which is the work's top. The angle word is passed as `PARAM WireAngle`, signed by the side rule and computed from the path. No U/V words are written.
  - The cone's turning moves are not sent, because the control makes them itself.
  - `taper_on` and the angle word are written before the lead-in, and `taper_off` before the lead-out.
  - A machine that states neither `uv` nor `edm.taper_angle` is refused by name.
  - The new PARAMs are listed in `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md`.
- The decision record is `docs/decisions/1164-wire-taper-angle-word.md`.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/wire_taper_angle.rs` (new):
  - `an_angle_word_punch_posts_its_golden_with_the_mitre_rule`: new NC golden `tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_taper_angle_punch.nc`; the CL equals `wire_taper_punch.cl`; the sign flips under `top_right`.
  - `the_cone_rule_turns_the_wire_about_each_corner`: the lean is held at 3 degrees through every corner, and the NC equals the mitre golden except for the note line.
  - `a_corner_the_stated_rule_gouges_blocks_the_post`: on a 3-degree drafted punch with sharp corners, the mitre rule verifies clean and posts. The cone rule's rounded lower corners gouge it, so the post is blocked with `wire gouge`.
  - `an_incomplete_dialect_and_a_four_axis_angle_cut_are_refused_by_name`: a missing corner rule, a missing side rule, neither uv nor angle, and 4-axis on an angle machine.
- `motion` unit test `the_cone_rule_holds_the_lean_and_refuses_a_lead_into_a_corner`; `post` unit test `taper_angle_words_parse_and_garbled_ones_refuse_the_file`.
- U/V goldens: `wire_taper`, `wire_4axis`, `wire_post`, `wire_contour` and `wire_verify` pass with their goldens unedited.
- Merge-time refresh (merge of upstream main df90b031, head 9673a77e): `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green (3 steps, 0 failed, 21.1 min; 3215 tests passed); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; golden `wire_taper_angle_punch.nc` unchanged.
- Gate on the pre-refresh head 39d014d8: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/537-wire-4axis` green (3 steps, 0 failed, 11.2 min); the wire suites by hand (wire_taper 5, wire_4axis 6, wire_post 5, wire_contour 7, wire_verify 3, wire_taper_angle 4: all pass); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- No real EDM control (D10). The angle code and dialect words are invented on the synthetic fixture.
- How a real control ramps the lean over the lead-in and lead-out is modelled as a linear ramp, the same as #536. The decision record states this.
- The `arc` corner rule (lean change rounded over a stated radius) is not offered.
- No UI page field for `edm.taper_angle`. It is machine-file data only, like `edm.codes`.
